description: A three-panel composite figure in which each panel is a dual-axis line plot of phase fraction versus true strain, comparing three annealing conditions. Every panel shares the same axis naming: the x-axis is "True strain"; the left black y-axis is "Fraction of DIM (%)" (deformation-induced martensite) and the right red y-axis is "Fraction of RA (%)" (retained austenite). (a) AN750-T: DIM axis 0-4.8 % with ticks every 0.8, RA axis 2-7 % with unit ticks, data plotted to a true strain of about 0.20; the rising black DIM curve flattens toward saturation and is marked by an arrow annotated "4.74%", while the red RA curve starts highest near zero strain and falls monotonically. (b) AN800-T: DIM axis 0-1.2 %, RA axis 1.2-2.4 %, strain only to about 0.07, DIM annotated "1.16%". (c) AN850-T: DIM axis 0-0.30 %, RA axis 0.30-0.60 %, strain to about 0.06, DIM annotated "0.28%". In all three panels the RA curve decreases while DIM increases, i.e. austenite is consumed by strain-induced martensite. The annotated final DIM fractions fall steeply with increasing annealing temperature (4.74 → 1.16 → 0.28 %) and the fracture strain range collapses, so the figure demonstrates that higher annealing temperature leaves far less retained austenite available for transformation.

subfigures.description: Dual-axis plot for AN750-T. Left black axis 'Fraction of DIM (%)' 0-4.8; right red axis 'Fraction of RA (%)' 2-7; x-axis 'True strain' to about 0.20. Black DIM curve rises and saturates, arrow-annotated '4.74%'; red RA curve declines monotonically from about 7 % toward about 2.5 %.

Dual-axis plot for AN800-T. Left black axis 'Fraction of DIM (%)' 0-1.2; right red axis 'Fraction of RA (%)' 1.2-2.4; x-axis 'True strain' to about 0.07. Black DIM curve rises to an arrow-annotated '1.16%'; red RA curve declines from about 2.4 % to about 1.2 %.

Dual-axis plot for AN850-T. Left black axis 'Fraction of DIM (%)' 0-0.30; right red axis 'Fraction of RA (%)' 0.30-0.60; x-axis 'True strain' to about 0.06. Black DIM curve rises to an arrow-annotated '0.28%'; red RA curve declines from about 0.60 % to about 0.33 %.

observations.observation: Each of the three panels plots a black curve labelled 'Fraction of DIM (%)' against a red curve labelled 'Fraction of RA (%)', both versus 'True strain' on a dual y-axis layout.
Panel (a) AN750-T: left DIM axis spans 0 to 4.8 % and right RA axis spans 2 to 7 %; the black DIM curve rises and flattens, with an arrow annotation reading 4.74%.
Panel (b) AN800-T: left DIM axis spans 0 to 1.2 % and right RA axis spans 1.2 to 2.4 %; the black DIM curve carries an arrow annotation reading 1.16%.
Panel (c) AN850-T: left DIM axis spans 0 to 0.30 % and right RA axis spans 0.30 to 0.60 %; the black DIM curve carries an arrow annotation reading 0.28%.

In all three panels the red retained-austenite curve decreases monotonically with true strain while the black deformation-induced-martensite curve increases and saturates, i.e. RA is consumed as DIM forms.
The annotated maximum DIM fraction drops from 4.74% for AN750-T to 1.16% for AN800-T to 0.28% for AN850-T, i.e. it falls by roughly an order of magnitude between 750 and 800 °C.

The right-hand RA axis scale of each panel is very different: 2-7 % in (a), 1.2-2.4 % in (b) and 0.30-0.60 % in (c), indicating that the retained-austenite content itself becomes far smaller at higher annealing temperature.
The true-strain range of the plotted data also shrinks from about 0.20 in (a) to about 0.07 in (b) and about 0.06 in (c).

The caption states the panels show deformation-induced martensite and retained austenite volume fraction changes based on the O-C (Olson-Cohen) model, and labels (a) AN750-T, (b) AN800-T, (c) AN850-T.

The citing text states the Olson-Cohen fitting parameters are alpha = 5, beta = 1.28, n = 0.55, with f_RA,0 the RA content before deformation and epsilon the true strain; these parameter values are not printed on any panel.
No error bars, residual curves or goodness-of-fit statistics are shown in any panel; the curves are smooth model fits rather than plotted data points.
